items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone Versus Standard Care in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares a new drug combination (xaluritamig plus abiraterone) against standard treatments in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who haven't received chemotherapy yet. The study is currently recruiting patients and will measure overall survival as the main outcome. This represents a potential new first-line treatment option for this patient population.

items.title: Lutetium-177-TLX591 Plus Standard Care in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial tests a radioligand therapy (177Lu-TLX591) combined with standard treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have already progressed after androgen receptor pathway inhibitor treatment. The trial is recruiting and evaluates both effectiveness and safety. This is another targeted radiation therapy option similar to Pluvicto.

items.title: Apalutamide and Targeted Radiation After Surgery for Recurrent Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial tests whether adding enhanced therapy (apalutamide with abiraterone) to standard radiation and hormone therapy works better than standard treatment alone in patients whose prostate cancer has returned after surgery. The study also tests whether adding radiation targeting metastases seen on PET scans provides additional benefit. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Testosterone and ZEN-3694 Combination in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial tests a novel approach using testosterone combined with ZEN-3694 (a drug targeting MYC protein) followed by enzalutamide plus ZEN-3694 in treatment-resistant castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to determine if initial testosterone dosing can make subsequent treatments more effective. This represents an innovative approach to overcoming resistance.

items.title: First-in-Human Study of GSK5471713 in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial evaluates a new drug called GSK5471713 given alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. The study will assess safety, how the body processes the drug, and early signs of effectiveness. Currently recruiting patients for this early-stage investigation of a novel therapy.

items.title: GSK5458514 Alone or Combined With Other Drugs in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 study tests GSK5458514, a new investigational drug, given alone or with other anti-cancer treatments in prostate cancer patients. The trial includes dose-finding and expansion phases to determine safe and effective dosing. Currently recruiting participants.

items.title: Adding Docetaxel for Patients Not Responding Well to Apalutamide
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial tests whether adding chemotherapy (docetaxel) helps patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer who don't achieve deep PSA response after starting apalutamide and hormone therapy. The study compares continuing apalutamide alone versus adding docetaxel. This addresses treatment intensification based on early response markers.

items.title: ABBV-969 Safety and Effectiveness Study in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial evaluates ABBV-969, an investigational drug given intravenously, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will determine safe doses and assess early effectiveness. Approximately 230 patients will be enrolled worldwide in dose-finding and dose-confirmation phases.

items.title: PSMA-Targeted Radiation Therapy in Low-Volume Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial compares standard hormone therapy alone versus combined with 177Lu-PSMA-617 (a targeted radiation treatment), with or without abiraterone, in patients with newly diagnosed or recurrent low-volume metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study tests whether adding targeted radiation improves outcomes in patients with limited metastatic disease.

items.title: Tarlatamab for DLL3-Positive Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial tests tarlatamab in patients with DLL3-positive prostate cancer that has spread and either returned after treatment or not responded to treatment. The study seeks to determine if this immunotherapy drug is effective against this specific biomarker-defined subset of aggressive prostate cancer.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Combinations in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 study tests ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate, given alone or combined with other treatments in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will assess safety, determine safe combination doses, and measure PSA response as an indicator of effectiveness.

items.title: Mevrometostat Study in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer and Other Cancers
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial evaluates mevrometostat, an investigational drug, in patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed after prior treatment. Part 3 of the study includes testing mevrometostat alone or combined with enzalutamide. The trial is currently recruiting men with previously treated CRPC.

items.title: Personalized Dosing Schedule for Lutetium-177 PSMA Radioligand Therapy
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares standard fixed-interval dosing of lutetium 177 Lu PSMA RLT versus a personalized schedule that adapts to each patient's response. The study aims to determine if lengthening intervals between doses based on individual response can improve quality of life while maintaining effectiveness in hormone-resistant metastatic prostate cancer.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Versus Chemotherapy in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate, to standard chemotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The primary goal is to determine if patients receiving I-DXd live longer overall and live longer without cancer progression compared to chemotherapy. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Inflammation Pathways Drive Treatment Resistance in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research paper describes how chronic inflammation activates specific signaling pathways (NFκB and JAK/STAT3) that work together with androgen receptor signaling to promote prostate cancer progression and treatment resistance. The study shows these inflammatory pathways cause epigenetic changes that help tumors survive, grow, spread, and evade the immune system, particularly in castration-resistant disease.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Boosts Immune Response and Checkpoint Inhibitor Effectiveness
items.summary: This preclinical study developed a DNA vaccine targeting PSMA (a protein highly expressed on prostate cancer cells) that stimulates strong immune responses. When combined with PD-1 checkpoint blockade immunotherapy, the vaccine enhanced tumor elimination and prevented lung metastases in experimental models, suggesting a potential strategy to overcome resistance to immunotherapy.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes Treatment Resistance in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Researchers developed a new drug that simultaneously blocks two important cancer pathways (BRD4 and AKT) to overcome resistance to AKT inhibitors in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study found that elevated c-MYC protein drives resistance to AKT inhibitors alone, and blocking both targets together more effectively stops cancer growth in laboratory studies.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This analysis of 21 clinical trials involving 1,580 patients examined the effectiveness of immune checkpoint inhibitors in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer without biomarker selection. The study found modest overall survival (63% at 1 year, 39% at 2 years) and better outcomes when checkpoint inhibitors were combined with other treatments rather than used alone.

items.title: New Detection Method for PSA and Cancer Biomarkers
items.summary: Scientists developed a highly sensitive test that can simultaneously detect two cancer markers (PSA for prostate cancer and AFP for liver cancer) in the same sample using quantum dot technology. This technical advancement could improve early cancer detection through more sensitive and efficient blood tests, though it requires clinical validation.

items.title: Targeting Regulatory T Cells in Prostate Cancer Immunotherapy
items.summary: This review examines how regulatory T cells (Tregs) in the tumor environment help prostate cancer evade the immune system. Research shows that high levels of activated Tregs in the tumor stroma are associated with more aggressive disease and higher recurrence risk. The paper discusses emerging therapeutic strategies to target these cells to improve immunotherapy effectiveness.

items.title: Zoledronic Acid Protects Bone Health During Enzalutamide Treatment
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial (BonEnza study) found that adding zoledronic acid to androgen deprivation therapy plus enzalutamide significantly prevented bone density loss in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients. After 18 months, patients receiving zoledronic acid maintained bone density at the femoral neck and lumbar spine, while those without it experienced significant bone loss.
